cues.en: So let's also talk about generative adversarial networks or GANS for short.
cues.zh: 也來談生成對抗網路，簡稱 GAN。

cues.en: This is a technology behind deep fakes and all those viral apps on your phone that do face swapping and aging, and all that fun stuff for turning you into cartoons.
cues.zh: 這是 Deepfake，以及手機上那些換臉、變老、把你變成卡通等熱門應用背後的技術。

cues.en: So very hot area of research, but it has, you know, actual useful applications as well.
cues.zh: 研究非常熱門，但也有真正實用的應用。

cues.en: And not just entertainment value.
cues.zh: 不只有娛樂價值。

cues.en: Although, you know, this is an example of a GAN that's been trained to generate random images of faces.
cues.zh: 這是訓練來隨機生成人臉影像的 GAN 範例。

cues.en: And that's the example we're going to dive into here in some depth.
cues.zh: 接著會深入研究這個例子。

cues.en: That's actually a picture of someone who does not exist.
cues.zh: 這其實是一個不存在的人。

cues.en: So by just training a generative adversarial network on how to make believable images of human faces, it got this good.
cues.zh: 只要訓練 GAN 生成可信的人臉，就能好到這種程度。

cues.en: I cannot tell the difference there myself.
cues.zh: 我自己分不出來。

cues.en: Well, let's talk about how they work.
cues.zh: 談談如何運作。

cues.en: So, yeah, I mean, it is a tech behind a bunch of this viral stuff.
cues.zh: 它確實是許多熱門應用背後的技術。

cues.en: It might just seem like a trend or a sort of a toy thing or at worst, you know, something that can be used for deception and deep fakes.
cues.zh: 可能看起來只是風潮或玩具，最糟是用來欺騙、做 Deepfake。

cues.en: But it actually has real practical applications as well.
cues.zh: 但其實也有真正實務應用。

cues.en: One is generating synthetic data sets if you have private information.
cues.zh: 例如，有私人資訊時，產生合成資料集。

cues.en: So this is very important in the medical field.
cues.zh: 在醫療領域很重要。

cues.en: If you're trying to train a model to detect if a biopsy is malignant or benign, for example, you don't want to be using real data because there's going to be a lot of privacy associated with that data.
cues.zh: 例如訓練模型，偵測切片是惡性還是良性，不希望直接用真實資料，因為有很多隱私問題。

cues.en: However, if you can train a GAN using real data, you can then generate synthetic data sets that are indistinguishable from a real one and use that in turn to train your models without any privacy concerns.
cues.zh: 但如果用真實資料訓練 GAN，就能產生與真實資料無法區分的合成資料集，再訓練模型，不必擔心隱私。

cues.en: They can also be used for anomaly detection.
cues.zh: 也能用來做異常偵測。

cues.en: So a side effect of a GANS, we will see, is a system that can tell the difference between a real and a fake image or whatever it is that you're dealing with.
cues.zh: 稍後會看到，GAN 的副產品，是能區分真實、假影像，或其他資料真假的系統。

cues.en: And you can use that to automatically detect things that are anomalous, things that don't look like they're supposed to look.
cues.zh: 可以利用它，自動偵測異常，也就是外觀不符合預期的東西。

cues.en: They also have applications in self-driving cars and more aesthetically in art and music.
cues.zh: 也能用在自駕車，以及更有美感的藝術與音樂。

cues.en: So you've probably seen demos of artificial intelligence that can generate its own symphonies in the style of Beethoven or Mozart or whatever, or that can generate paintings in the style of Picasso or
cues.zh: 你可能看過 AI 示範，能以 Beethoven、Mozart 等風格，自行產生交響樂，或以 Picasso，

cues.en: your favorite impressionistic painter.
cues.zh: 或你喜歡的印象派畫家風格作畫。

cues.en: Those are all GANs that work where they've been trained to produce convincing fakes of whatever data you can dream up.
cues.zh: 這些都是 GAN，經訓練後，能針對任何你想得到的資料，產生令人信服的仿作。

cues.en: So how do they work?
cues.zh: 如何運作？

cues.en: Well, let's dive into it.
cues.zh: 深入看看。

cues.en: So the what a GAN is trying to do is learn the actual distribution of these latent vectors that make
cues.zh: GAN 想學的是，構成真實影像、資料集、音樂或藝術作品等內容的潛在向量，

cues.en: up a real image or data set or music or artwork, whatever it might be.
cues.zh: 真正的分布。

cues.en: And it's kind of built on the idea of something called a variation auto encoder or a VAE.
cues.zh: 有點建立在變分自編碼器，也就是 VAE 的概念上。

cues.en: One of the main differences between VAEs is that a VAE assumes a Gaussian normal distribution in the the latent features that it's learning, whereas a GAN can learn anything.
cues.zh: 與 VAE 的主要差異之一，是 VAE 假設學到的潛在特徵，服從高斯常態分布，GAN 則能學任何分布。

cues.en: So it's not really as restricted.
cues.zh: 因此，限制沒那麼多。

cues.en: But again, a little bit too technical there, I think.
cues.zh: 不過，我想有點太技術性。

cues.en: So if you got to be generating random faces in this example, your input is actually going to be random noise and it's going to learn how to turn that random noise into a random face that is a believable
cues.zh: 這個隨機人臉例子，輸入其實是隨機雜訊，它會學習把雜訊，轉成可信的隨機

cues.en: face.
cues.zh: 人臉。

cues.en: How's that work?
cues.zh: 怎麼做？

cues.en: Well, at the same time, we have this discriminator here that's learning how to tell real images from fake images.
cues.zh: 同時，這裡有判別器，學習分辨真實與假影像。

cues.en: So if we back up a little bit here, we have this generator that's being trained on how to convince realistic fakes.
cues.zh: 退一步，有一個生成器，訓練來產生可信的仿真影像。

cues.en: Its job is to try to fool the discriminator into thinking that it's fake faces or real faces.
cues.zh: 任務是欺騙判別器，讓它以為假人臉是真人臉。

cues.en: And if it's starting off by generating a face that looks like Tweety Bird, the discriminator will probably learn pretty quickly that that's not a real face and classify that is fake.
cues.zh: 如果一開始，生成的臉像崔弟鳥，判別器很快就會學會，那不是真人臉，分類為假。

cues.en: Meanwhile, we're fitting the discriminator real faces as well so we can actually train this discriminator on how well it's classifying these images coming in as real or fake because we know if they're actually
cues.zh: 同時，也餵給判別器真人臉，因此能根據它將影像分成真或假的表現訓練，因為我們知道資料究竟

cues.en: real or actually fake.
cues.zh: 是真還是假。

cues.en: At the same time, though, the generator is trying to fool the discriminator.
cues.zh: 但同時，生成器也試著欺騙判別器。

cues.en: So it's being measured on its ability to get the discriminator to say, yeah, I think your image was real.
cues.zh: 衡量的是，能否讓判別器說：「對，我覺得你的影像是真的。」

cues.en: So these things are in tension with each other.
cues.zh: 因此，兩者互相抗衡。

cues.en: That's why they call it an adversarial network.
cues.zh: 所以叫對抗網路。

cues.en: The generator is trying to fool the discriminator, the discriminators, trying to uncover the generator and it's deception.
cues.zh: 生成器試著欺騙判別器，判別器試著揭穿生成器的欺騙。

cues.en: So this is a very complicated thing to train.
cues.zh: 訓練非常複雜。

cues.en: But you can see the power of this where we have these two neural networks being trained simultaneously in tension with each other.
cues.zh: 但可以看到，兩個神經網路同時訓練、互相抗衡的力量。

cues.en: And that really pushes the generator into getting very good at producing realistic looking fakes.
cues.zh: 這真的推動生成器，變得很擅長產生逼真的仿作。

cues.en: So just to recap, again, the generators job is to try to fool the discriminator into thinking that the images it's making is real and at the same time, the discriminator is trying to catch the generator
cues.zh: 再次回顧，生成器想欺騙判別器，讓它認為產生的影像是真的；同時，判別器想抓到生成器

cues.en: in the act.
cues.zh: 造假的證據。

cues.en: So as you both get better and better with more training over time, are discriminator gets better and better at detecting fakes and the generator gets better and better at making fakes.
cues.zh: 隨著訓練、兩者不斷進步，判別器越來越會辨假，生成器越來越會造假。

cues.en: And again, they are adversarial.
cues.zh: 再次強調，兩者是對抗關係。

cues.en: Hence the name generative adversarial network.
cues.zh: 所以叫生成對抗網路。

cues.en: And once you get to a point where the discriminator can't really tell the difference anymore, you know, you're pretty much done with training.
cues.zh: 到判別器再也分不太出真假的時候，訓練大致完成。

cues.en: One thing we're talking about in the context of images is something called the transposed convolution.
cues.zh: 影像情境中，要談一個叫做轉置卷積的東西。

cues.en: So a discriminator might be using a straight up, confused layer like we looked at and seasons to try to boil an image down to its latent features.
cues.zh: 判別器可能用一般 Conv2D 層，像 CNN 介紹的那樣，把影像濃縮為潛在特徵。

cues.en: But the generators job is to create new images from a lower representation of the data, specifically a a little vector of random noise.
cues.zh: 但生成器要從較低維度的資料表示，具體來說，是一個小的隨機雜訊向量，建立新影像。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: So how does that work?
cues.zh: 如何運作？

cues.en: Well, it turns out there's something called a confused transpose layer, which is just the inverse of a transpose layer.
cues.zh: 有一種 Conv2DTranspose 層，可以把它想成卷積層的反向操作。

cues.en: So instead of trying to reduce image down into a lower dimensional representation, a confused transpose layer is trying to build up a larger image.
cues.zh: 不再將影像縮成低維表示，而是試著建立更大的影像。

cues.en: So it's learning these weights that are used to reconstruct a larger image from a smaller image.
cues.zh: 因此，學習的是用來從較小影像，重建較大影像的權重。

cues.en: And again, this could be used on more than just images, but typically that's the context.
cues.zh: 同樣，不只影像能用，但通常會在影像情境看到。

cues.en: You'll see it in often easy to strive to, although sometimes we'll see interleaving of strides in one in two different layers of the of the actual model.
cues.zh: 通常會看到步長二，但有時，模型不同層會交錯使用步長一與二。

cues.en: And if you're going to be doing this, you can also use something called Max Unpooling, which is the inverse of max pooling.
cues.zh: 也能使用 Max Unpooling，也就是最大池化的反向操作。

cues.en: So basically, think of it as a CNN that works backwards and this can live within the generator.
cues.zh: 基本上，把它想成反向運作的 CNN，可以放在生成器內。

cues.en: The fancy math behind this whole thing, behind GAN, is this, and I'm not going to go into too much depth, but the first part of it is worth talking about.
cues.zh: GAN 背後的數學公式是這個，不會深入，但第一部分值得談。

cues.en: So this is the adversarial lost function.
cues.zh: 這是對抗損失函數。

cues.en: And basically, we call this a min-max game because it's starting off with min and Max.
cues.zh: 基本上，叫做最小最大賽局，因為開頭是 min 與 max。

cues.en: So the min sub g indicates that the generator is trying to minimize its loss in creating realistic images and fooling the discriminator. And the max of D,
cues.zh: min 下標 G，表示生成器想最小化產生逼真影像、欺騙判別器的損失；max 下標 D，

cues.en: it means that the discriminator at the same time is maximizing its ability to detect the fakes.
cues.zh: 表示判別器同時最大化辨識假資料的能力。

cues.en: So again, this whole thing is very complicated and delicate.
cues.zh: 再次強調，整件事非常複雜、精細。

cues.en: The the training is very unstable and there's a lot of hyper parameters involved.
cues.zh: 訓練很不穩定，而且涉及很多超參數。

cues.en: You get one wrong, you're not going to have a stable system when you're training it.
cues.zh: 只要一個錯，就無法穩定訓練。

cues.en: There's also a lot of trial and error involved just in getting the topology right and just seeing what works through experimentation.
cues.zh: 也需要大量反覆試驗，才能找對拓樸，透過實驗知道什麼有效。

cues.en: So it's a very fragile thing to train, which is a very much a downside of this stuff.
cues.zh: 因此，訓練很脆弱，這是很大的缺點。

cues.en: It's also very resource intensive, as we'll soon find out.
cues.zh: 也很耗資源，很快會發現。

cues.en: It's also subject to a problem called mode collapse.
cues.zh: 另外，還有模式崩塌問題。

cues.en: So if you have different types of faces, you know, say different races, for example, you can see where I'm going here from an ethical standpoint, a GAN can still be very successful by just learning how
cues.zh: 如果有不同類型的人臉，例如不同族群，從倫理角度應該知道我要說什麼；GAN 只要學會

cues.en: to successfully create one specific type of whatever it is you're doing.
cues.zh: 成功產生某一種特定類型，也可能非常成功。

cues.en: So maybe it just gets really good at making images of white people.
cues.zh: 也許最後只很擅長產生白人人像。

cues.en: Right.
cues.zh: 對吧？

cues.en: Or maybe if you're trying to train how to make images of clothing, it can get really successful by making images of shirts and nothing else.
cues.zh: 或者訓練生成服裝影像，卻只靠產生襯衫，就獲得成功，其他都不生成。

cues.en: That's what we call mode collapse.
cues.zh: 這叫模式崩塌。

cues.en: So in a case where it converges on making just one type of thing really well, that's kind of a way for the GAN to cheat, but something to watch out for sure.
cues.zh: 收斂到只會非常好地做一種東西，有點像 GAN 作弊，但確實要注意。

cues.en: It can lead to a model that's not really as general-purpose as you might think, or at worst might lead to some sort of a, you know, unintentional bias in how you're applying the model.
cues.zh: 它可能讓模型沒有想像中通用，最糟甚至讓應用模型時，產生無意偏差。

cues.en: They're also very subject to vanishing gradients and the vanishing gradient problem.
cues.zh: 也很容易受到梯度消失問題影響。

cues.en: They're just really, really touchy things to train.
cues.zh: 訓練真的非常敏感。

cues.en: So with that, let's go through an actual notebook and see it in action, but but first I want to go through some Hands-On examples of using GANS just so you get a better feel of how they're actually trained
cues.zh: 接著，透過真正的 Notebook 看實際運作，但先做幾個 GAN 實作範例，讓你更了解它們實際如何訓練，

cues.en: and applied in the real world.
cues.zh: 以及如何應用在真實世界。
